Ideally, both 'Fill Flash', which has 'Strength' and 'Saturation' slider settings, and 'Fill Light/Clarity', which has 'Fill Light' and 'Clarity' slider settings, should be combined into a single tool window containing three or four sliders, instead of confusing users as to which of these two tools to use.

ѾѾ The software links to a variety of searchable online help and built-in tutorials. As with some of their other recent software releases, including the previous PSP X4, Corel has the help documentation in this PSP X5 set up so that clicking on the 'Help' option from the menu and then selecting 'Help Topics' starts up your browser and takes you to Corel's Web site where all of the help topics are accessible online and can also be searched. I really wished that Corel gave the user the option, during the initial software CD installation process, to either install the entire help documentation locally on the computer or to link the software to Corel's online Web site. After all, being dependent upon online access in order to access help information can be problematic if the user needs to search the 'Help Topics' from a place where there is no Internet access. On October 2 2012, Corel released a 76-MB 'PSPX5_LocalHelp.exe' patch that does install all of the help files locally on the computer, but after I installed this patch, clicking the 'Help Topics' still always brings up my browser and opens up a new Web page to display Corel's online help content. And there does not seem to be a way to configure PSP X5 to default to offline mode and use the locally-installed help files even when no Internet connection is available. But you can still manually access the locally-installed help files by directly pointing your browser at the directory path where all of the help files are installed. The main Web page for the help files is located in the directory path below:

32-bit C:\Program Files\Corel\Corel PaintShop Pro X5\Languages\EN\Help\wwhelp\wwhimpl\js\html\wwhelp.htm
64-bit: C:\Program Files (x86)\Corel\Corel PaintShop Pro X5\Languages\EN\Help\wwhelp\wwhimpl\js\html\wwhelp.htm

If your PSP install also constantly redirects you to Corel's Web site after installing the help files locally, you can point your Web browser to this location to access the locally-installed help files. This locally-installed help documentation page, complete with a search function, works well using either Internet Explorer or Safari browsers, but Firefox just displays a blank two-framed page.

Ѿ My one main gripe about this and all previous versions of PSP is that it still does not have a tool for stitching together panoramic photos. Photoshop has the \\"Photomerge\\" utility and Canon has \\"PhotoStitch\\" for creating panorama photos. But PaintShop Pro and also Corel's Photo-Paint in their Graphics Suite package have been missing this very useful functionality for a long time. Corel really needs to add a panorama merge/stitch function to their ever-increasing rich set of tools. The current way to create a panoramic photo in PSP is an entirelymanual and laborious process. You first create a new canvas that is large enough to hold all of the expected overlapping photos, you then copy each photo into a separate layer, decrease the opacity of one layer so you can see through it while you manually move the layer around to visually align the edges of one photo with the overlapping portion of another photo, and you repeat this tedious process for all overlapping photos that will be used in the panorama before setting the layers' opacities back to 100%. Needless to say, this is both time-consuming and highly prone to error, and the manually merged result only works if you shot the overlapping photos using a tripod with a panning head and a very level camera. By comparison, Canon's \\"PhotoStitch\\" program is very user-friendly and flexible with its options, and it automatically aligns and merges photos in the order that you specify.

► Performance, Stability, Reliability: ѾѾѾѾѾ Excellent 5-fuzzies rating

ѾѾѾѾѾ Compared to previous versions of PSP, this X5 version has pretty good stability. During almost one year of weekly usage before writing this review, I have had the software crash or hang about 3 or 4 times total, and this includes running the software on an old underpowered Windows Vista laptop and a tiny Windows 7 Dell Mini 10 netbook. Corel has obviously worked on adding stability with this version, along with GPU optimizations.

ѾѾѾѾѾ Speed has been noticeably improved, the performance is considerably faster than previous versions, start-up time to launch the program for the first time has been improved, and these improvements are especially apparent when running PSP X5 on an older slower computer. When used on my 5-year old Windows Vista laptop with 2GB memory, applying most effects happens in real-time, and for some operations such as adjusting sharpening parameters on 100-MB TIFF image files, the pop-up preview window will still display a progress meter, but these progress meters only last for a few seconds on this older laptop of mine.

ѾѾѾѾѾ This X5 version uses less than 400 MB of disk space on a full install. The previous X4 version used about 900 MB of disk space, and version X3 required 3GB of disk space, which tells me that prior to X4, PSP had become very bloated and disorganized. So this redesign both increased performance and reduced the disk space required. By comparison, Adobe's Photoshop Elements 11 requires a whopping 3GB to 4GB of disk space, even though it has less features and effects than PSP.

► Competitive Pricing & Value: ѾѾѾѾѾ Excellent 5-fuzzies rating

ѾѾѾѾѾ At the time of this review's writing, PaintShop Pro X5 Ultimate is being discounted on Amazon at a price less than $50, and its price is less than Amazon's price for Photoshop Elements 11, even though PSPX4 is a more capable and better program! With the Amazon discounting, this is truly a bargain for the amount of photo and graphics editing power that you get.

௫ Fuzzy Wuzzy's Conclusion:

For overall bang-for-the-buck combination of very affordable value and feature-packed power in a commercial photo-editing software package, this PSP X5 currently reigns supreme, beating out Adobe Photoshop Elements 11 and all other photo-editing software that I can think of. If you want something even less expensive, look into a freeware graphics software called \\"GIMP\\" which offers a ton of graphics editing power for free. And if you have no experience with graphics software or if you do not want to spend time learning its complexities, look into the free and easy-to-use software called \\"Paint.NET\\".

Despite the significant performance improvements in versions X4 and X5 (they are roughly 50% to 100% faster than X3 and also far more stable), it still does have its slow areas of laggardly performance. In particular, this is not a good software for processing RAW files, both dueto its slow RAW converter and due to its limited RAW compatibility.

If you want the deluxe photo management and editing solution, deluxe in capability, cost, and complexity, using Adobe's Lightroom and Photoshop CS are the way to go. Otherwise, this PSP X5 is an excellent \\"Photoshop for the masses\\" alternative. If you primarily shoot in RAW, adding Corel's AfterShot Pro allows for great RAW handling followed by photo editing in PSP X5. And if Corel's HDR feature in PSP X5 has whetted your appetite for HDR processing, you should seriously consider getting Photomatix Pro (currently at version 4) since its capabilities exceed anything that Corel or Adobe has to offer.

If you are using a version of PaintShop Pro prior to X4, is this PSP X5 worth the upgrade?

Most definitely! There were many dozens of improvements in going from X3 to X4. Even if you ignore all of its new features and enhancements, just the fact that X4 and X5 run a lot faster and are more stable than X3 is a compelling enough reason to upgrade. However, the improvements in going from X4 to X5 are more incremental; there were far more improvements in going from X3 to X4. But with a good discounted price, it is still worthy upgrading from X4 to X5.

If you are just starting out with photo-editing, should you buy this PSP X5 or Adobe Photoshop Elements 11?

I feel that PSP X5 is a far more capable and feature-rich program than Adobe Photoshop Elements 11. PSP X5 is more like the full-blown Photoshop CS version than APE11. APE11 includes more built-in layer styles that PSP X5 does not have, although if you are just starting out, you will not miss this. Once you become proficient in PSP X5, you can create your own styles and record them as scripts to repeatedly reuse. Photoshop Elements has a much larger user base than PSP, and there are numerous sites to download brushes and textures from, but it is easy to convert Photoshop brushes to use in PSP, so thatis not really a problem. APE11 has more adjustment brushes than PSP X5 when it comes to brushing on effects like dodge, burn, and saturation. But PSP X5 has more artistic tools than APE11, useful for painting, drawing, scrapbooking, and graphic design, and PSP X5 is more useful and flexible for manipulating images other than photos than APE11. PSP X5 requires less than one third the disk space to install than APE11, and at the time of this review's writing, Amazon has it priced lower than APE11, even though PSP X5 is far more packed with features. But... if you think that you will eventually migrate up to Photoshop CS, which is far more complex, powerful, and expensive, then starting out with APE11 will give you skills that are more transferable to Photoshop CS than becoming proficient with PSP X5.

One final note: On August 2013, Corel released a \\"Service Pack 3\\" patch that provides various enhancements and bug fixes. After installing PaintShop Pro X5 on your computer, you can either download this 98-MB executable from Corel's Web site, or from the user interface, click 'Help' and \\"Check for Updates\\" to download and install the service pack that way. You should definitely install this service pack .

review_headline: Badly Flawed Version of a Once-Great Program
review_body:
I'm a long-time fan of AnyTime Deluxe v8.5 and I love it! This review is for AnyTime Organizer Deluxe 14.

The familiar AnyTime screens are present (maybe too familiar since there has been very little graphic updating--it still looks like a Windows 98 program, which it was) and it did load my old .atw files (although it said it was converting them). The only reason I purchased this program was because it promised to sync my calendar with Google Calendar which I now use with my Android phone. I figured this would be the best of both worlds!

First problem, it would not sync and bombed with an error code. Their tech support (gotta give them credit, had an answer in less than an hour!) advised that I would have to run the program in Administrator mode. Any developer knows that Admin mode is something you only require for very specific tasks. This does not instill confidence since I must grant their software permission to do anything it likes to my system. That is a huge security hole and inexcusable in the 21st century.

Next problem, it appears that syncing is a special event, one which the user must affirmatively initiate. It just does not happen when the program is run or in the background. To add insult to injury, every time you want to sync you must resupply the program with your Google login and password. Imagine using this program every day and being forced to provide login credentials each time. That was the last straw. I reverted back to an earlier Windows restore point and copied my old .atw files over from last night's backup.

Oh, and one more thing. The Google sync was far from complete. Some days that had four events in them on my Google calendar showed up as blank in AnyTime. It did bring over some events, but I was hard-pressed to figure out what criteria the software used. Another issue was that, with the exception of scheduled events, the sync only brought in recent events. In this case, it appeared that it was only concerned with December (the month I am writing this review).

One star might be a harsh review since the bulk of the program seems to perform well (calendar, address book, etc.) but these functions are widely available elsewhere for free. As a legacy user of the program, I was looking to keep using it in the modern world. Sadly the software fails in many critical areas and is basically unusable to me. So, that's why I gave it one star.only concerned with December (the month I am writing this review).

review_headline: Something about you get what you pay for....
review_body:
I have been working on simple content websites for years using various products. My needs are simple - emphasis on simple - just several content pages connected by links. I decided to try WebEasy because of the lower cost. Right off, the product looks intuitive but it is really not. The learning curve is higher than what I expected. It can be hard to figure out basic structural activities so be prepared to do a lot of searching and reading even if you are well experienced in basic website development. After a couple of hours, I expected to have at least grasp the product's basic paradigm and methods, but felt like I did not understand how it really approached website development.

Do not consider this product if you desire to import an existing website. It didn't even come close to properly laying out the pages and setting the links. The makers of WebEasy claim importing websites is function of how well the websites are constructed. True but, when you are dealing with simple cleanly developed content pages that are properly rendered in the browsers of 30,000 people, I expect the import to be close. After all, Chrome, FireFox and Explorer got it right. WebEasy was so far off, the entire website had to be reconstructed from scratch because I didn't know where to being fixing all the issues. I did an sample import from a very basic website of four pages without special formatting or links. WebEasy did import 90% of it correctly and I could easily fix the broken links. Overall, it seems like the more pages the worse the import gets.

Annoyances: The various tool panes become undocked and float on top of the page in development with no way to dock or anchor the tool windows. I spent too much time moving panes around keeping them out of the way. A preview of a 12 page site took more than 10 minutes to load because it rebuilds the entire website even when there are no changes. Using the site map frequently crashed the application. There is no import from website. The website has to be downloaded externally first. Likewise, publishing a website is only to their hosting service. If do not use their service then you have to publish to your local computer and then manually copy to your website. You cannot publish individual pages again because it rebuilds everything all the time. Therefore every little change requires testing the entire website. There are global settings you can change at build, but the build starts automatically so you have to start stop the build change the settings and then restart the build.

It is a workable product, but I think WebEasy is best if you simply want to add your content to one of their existing templates. It does seem that per-developed templates for their hosting service is the real target for this application.

product_title: Learn Spanish: Fluenz Spanish Latin America 1+2+3+4+5 for Mac, PC, and Phone, Version 3
review_headline: Fun! Motivated me to actually stick with the lessons... and that's the bottom line!
review_body:
So many reviews have been written touching on all the specifics of this program, but an important point I want to stress is: Fluenz is a lot more fun than competing programs. I generally approve of their teaching style and specific choices, but what really sets this program apart is that I ACTUALLY sat down and did it every day, because it was sufficiently enjoyable and interesting to make me want to.

That's never happened before. Classes are just a beast to fit into my schedule, and other programs or audio that I checked out from the library just gathered dust after a few dull lessons. I test-drove RS but hated the approach. So I spent ten years saying \\"I should really get around to learning some Spanish,\\" then bought this program and *presto* I got around to it.

Some find Sonia (the tutor) annoying or cheesy but she really grew on me. I found I loved her cheerfulness and encouragement (and dorky jokes), especially because I worked on my lessons in the mornings and I do like to start my day on a positive note. The images and videos that some find superfluous do make the program visually enticing and less dull. I mean, there is a reason you didn't opt to pick up a textbook at a thrift store and memorize its contents. Good and appealing design will help you stick with the lessons. Selective content, repetition and the mix of audio and visual will make the material stick in your head. (Especially if you are a visual learner, like me.)

Basically Fluenz succeeded at:
1. getting me to do ALL the lessons
2. getting me to retain (like glue) the material they covered

....which isn't THAT much. And I think that is fine! I am by no means fluent, but I am comfortable enough with what I now know to not get flustered trying to remember it while someone waits for me to answer. NO ONE will ever get fluent alone in their living room. You have to be dealing with real-time, sink-or-swim conversation for that. Fortunately, this program is a wonderful foundation to build on. It is quite easy to then satisfy your thirst for more vocab. I now pick a topic every week (body parts! animals! professions! adjectives about personality! things you see in the grocery store! etc) and make a big list of new words to learn. So glad they focused on structures and situationally-appropriate vocab in the program. You will need to supplement as with any home learning system, but you will be glad you have this as a base. I loooove it. I am going to use it for other languages, for sure. So worth it.

product_title: Replay Now: East India Company [Gold Edition]
review_body:

I selected this version from TopWare Interactive because it came with a CD. I installed it onto Windows 7 platform and it required no patches or downloads. There have been no issues at all with platform stability or overall playability. I have played a lot of these types of games so the two tutorials it came with were good enough to get me started and use to the interface. They should have considered a little more depth in their tutorials for those that have never played this type of game.

The game has great graphics, nice looking ships and a timed released schedule of when they become available. I found the realism in the market prices to be refreshing after all if you flood the market with a product the prices will drop. So a little balance in the goods has to be thought out, planned and managed or you will find it difficult to make a lot of profit. The battles have two modes to choose from and this was probably the least desirable part of the game. It is difficult to control in both modes of battle and I found auto calculate was my best option. This is not so good if you enjoy controlling the battles but on a positive note auto calculate gives a very realistic outcome unlike other games. On the negative side of auto calculate you cannot capture and loot the other ships.

Port battles were very disappointing and remind me of the old Risk concept. They should have taken the time to put a little more depth in this part of the game. I am still pretty early in the game (1625) and have no trouble staying ahead of the AI in almost all phases of the game. Other reviews talk about not making a profit and I am not sure what they are doing as I have 7 fleets and over 6 million pounds in cash. I have not captured a port yet as my first attempt was an utter failure and the AI has had one country capture a port and another resign from the game.

Overall this is a good game but the map is very limited. I know this is the whole concept behind the game to focus on this region but it may limit re-playability. The game does get a little repetitive but that is no different than Port Royal or other similar games. If you are use to the short distance between ports from games like Patrician and Port Royal you may find this to be a much slower game. Also if you like devloping the ports you will be very disappointed in this part of the game as there are only a few key buildings and nothing else.

review_headline: Not sure that it even deserves this
review_body:
I ordered this direct from Serif. The main reason I ordered it was that Serif said that a hands-on manual was included, which it was.

I am giving it 2 stars, but I am not sure that it even deserves that many. There are many shortcomings to this program.

1. In creating a disk menu, there is no way that I have found to change the disk title. Just typing over the \\"My Title\\" like the manual says does nothing.

2. The manual gives no hint about how to change chapter titles. I found out on my own how to do it. One must right-click on the chapter thumbnail, and that takes you to a dialog box where you can change the chapter title.

3. I have been trying to burn a video which, according to the burn dialog box, is 4.29 gigs, onto a 4.7-gig disk. It won't burn.

4. The program shuts down arbitrarily. I try to burn at night while I am asleep and everything else is shut down on the machine. But in the morning when I check to see if the disk is done, I get an error message about Video Plus running into \\"unusual behavior\\" and shutting down. I am given no reason for the shut down.

5. For whatever reason, there is no indicator indicating the amount of DVD space that will be used for the project. Only the mention in the dialog box that I mentioned earlier. Such an indicator -- like virtually every other movie editing software has -- would be helpful in determining why I can't burn projects to disk with this program.

6. If you want to use this dog to edit a video file before putting it into a larger project, it will not save it as a video file. When you go to the folder where you thought that you have saved your video, you will find it saved as a project, not as an MP4 or other format file. This is disgusting.

7. When I installed it, I had to go online in order to \\"unlock\\" some features. I use it on a desktop which has Internet access and a laptop that doesn't. I should not have to goonline to \\"unlock\\" any features in order to use it on my laptop. The \\"unlock\\" function could have been put on the install disk quite easily, but yet was not. A very chintzy way to offer a software program to the public.

In summary, I would suggest that one look around and see what else is available before even considering a purchase of Movie Plus X5. I paid $20 to Serif for it, but in actual practice, it functions more like a crippled free version. There are other video editing software out there, and I would recommend that if one can afford to do so, that he get a higher-end product and use that. If one has to use Movie Plus X5 due to financial constraints -- all I can say is that you get what you pay for.

Update to the above review: On Friday, March 22, I uninstalled Movie Plus X5 and then re-installed. I tried it again last night, and I got the same error message that I got before I uninstalled it. This morning, I can't even get it to load! It's going to be deleted before the day is out.

Even though the program includes a manual, the manual is so awful that it is useless. There are tutorial videos included, but they aren't worth the disk space. This program cost me $20, but it isn't even worth 20 cents.

There are other video editing programs out there, and some of them are free. Plus Windows 7 has DVD Maker and Movie Maker included, so one doesn't need to waste his money on Serif's piece of trash. In view of these programs being readily available, the availability of free editing software on the web, and the trials that I have shared about using this program, anyone who still makes a conscious choice to buy this thing deserves whatever grief that he may experience from it. I would change the rating down to 1 star or even 0 stars, but the rating is locked in. So I will end by saying these three little words: I HATE IT!!

review_headline: An unfortunate misstep once again for Microsoft
review_body:
It seems that it usually takes Microsoft two tries to get things right with O/S's (operating systems) nowadays! Windows 7 righted the fiasco of Vista and hopefully by October of 2013 \\"Windows Blue\\" aka Windows 8.1 will right Windows 8 or Metro without additional charge.

What is good about Windows 8:

In one word: fast.

What is not so good about Windows 8: (oh boy...)

1. The Metro interface is a mess for use on a desktop! Touch screen and the Metro interface is fine for tablets and phones, but for a desktop, most people want ease of use and they just want it to work. Perhaps for a touch screen all in one computer, it might be ok. For a desktop with a keyboard, mouse, and monitor - Windows 8 is a nuisance. For many users who are upgrading, it is unfriendly and downright unusable. Unless you are a power user or someone who embraces new ideas quickly, Windows 8 in it's present format is probably not for you.

2. Microsoft doesn't seem to understand the basics of customer loyalty. It is a big mistake to take away something you gave in a previous O/S. Microsoft's ill conceived plan to leave out Windows Media Center and try to charge extra for it in Windows 8 (after the initial limited time give-away) is a huge mistake. There are indications this will be corrected in Windows 8.1 as well. Let's hope so!

Now for the big question: HOW CAN YOU FIX IT?

One way to overcome the Metro interface is to use a free and relatively simple program which restores the desktop interface. You can research these products by reviews on PCWORLD magazine online. (Like any other program, you use it at your own risk!) I chose a program called CLASSIC SHELL by the open source people at Sourceforge. I am not affiliated with them and I cannot make any statement as to its suitability for you or your computer. However, they are the people who have developed the popular open source programs VLC and 7-Zip. The program is working very well for me.

Anyway, if you upgraded or bought a new pc with Windows 8, don't panic! Once you get the desktop interface back, it is a reasonably good and stable O/S. Hopefully Microsoft has heard the outcry of their customers and have seen the plummeting sales of Windows 8 and new computers and will restore the ability to boot to the desktop interface and restore Windows Media Center as part of the O/S as well.

Happy computing!

Update: July 14, 2013. Although the Windows 8.1 update will be free, I still cannot recommend Windows 8 or 8.1 for the following reasons.

First, let the user decide whether they want to have a desktop or a mobile pc experience. This means fully restoring the desktop menu system rather than providing a semi-functional start button.

Second, Windows Media Center needs to be part of the operating system and not some very expensive extra cost add-on. Home theater computers are very popular and a great way to enjoy movies and music. Windows Media Center must be restored as a standard feature to Windows 8.

Unless Microsoft wakes up, the rate of adoption of Windows 8 will remain very low. It is much easier to migrate your Windows 7 operating system to the new computer rather than put up with the cumbersome mess that is Windows 8.

The games can be fun, but there are irksome deficiencies in the programming.  In spades:  one's partner, as often as an opponent,  will frequently take a high card,like a K that the player is depending on for a point. It's like the partner is playing against the human.  The partner will bid illogically.  If the partner has 6 spades, A, K, Q, 5, 3, 2, for example, it'll bid \\"6\\" on just having six spades notwithstanding the likelihood of the lower numbers being taken.  Also the idiot will pitch a K on the first round of a suit before the A has been played thus sacrificing a point either needed for its bid, or one than could have added to its bidding points.  All the electronic players are inclined to do that.  Sometimes I make a moderately high bid like \\"4\\" with two Aces and two Kings and then the partner might bid a ridiculously high bid that it can't meet in combination with mine and will break Spades on my K.  These characteristics are deliberately counterproductive to good play.  Thus the partner functions like a saboteur.  Winning at Spades is not too difficult but one must guard against the stupidity of one's partner.  Some electronic plays are outrageously poor.  I played a game in which I had bid nil before the partner bid 3.  On one hand knowing that it needed to protect its partner (me) it threw an Ace of Clubs away on a play of Hearts before knowing what I'd have to play thus endangering our position.  Later when Clubs were played my partner played its lowest Club, a 4, when it had a 9 and 7 in its hand.  I had to play a 6 which caused me to take the trick, thus losing my nil bid.  These types of stupid playing are inexcusable.  It is obviously a defect in the programming.  In Hearts:  the human player will be dealt the Q, K, A of Spades far oftener than should normally logically be likely.  There is a strange proclivity for the Q of Spades to be dropped when the suit of Clubs is played.  Also the hands dealt frequently have unnatural and highly unbalanceddistribution of suits.  It seems like the hands are deliberately distributed in an unnatural way and more often than not to the disadvantage of the human player. Winning at Hearts is difficult.  In Pitch:  most of the hands dealt will be of high face cards to the electronic opponents and of medium and low cards to the human.  When the electronic players get a biddable hand it will more often than not include an A and K and maybe a J and 10 or other low point throwaways.  The human will get either an A or a K and then some low point card.  The human can rarely safely bid even \\"2\\".  Either the electronic player will have bid before, or the hand will be too meager. It's amazing that a human can ever win at Pitch.

product_title: True Image Home 2012 PC Backup and Recovery [Old Version]
review_headline: Acronis True Image 2012 - A Great Product Keeps Getting Better
review_body:
Let me start this review with a little background about myself. I'm an experienced IT professional, with fourteen years experience. I've tried and used a large variety of software products because professionally I often find myself in situations where I need to do things sometimes considered impossible. But when your options are give up and spend sometimes hundreds of hours recreating something from scratch, or do the impossible, suddenly the impossible looks pretty appealing.

The Acronis line of products are among the best you'll find. I don't understand why they're ranked so low by other reviewers on Amazon. I've been using the Acronis line of products since their 2009 version, and the product line just keeps getting better. If you're looking for something that will do an absolutely bare metal restorable backup (i.e. you've lost your entire hard drive with no hope of recovering it) and you have a good backup of your PC, this is the product you want on your side. Professionally, I was first introduced to the Acronis product line when I was looking to go from a file only backup of my servers to a bare metal backup. Some of our servers require hundreds of hours to configure, so having a file level backup only wasn't good enough. I contacted Acronis and explained that I wanted to put their product to the test. At this point, let me explain that I tested their server line product, and now the PC line product, which the review is about, but they are almost exactly the same product. I explained that my test would involve using Acronis to perform a full backup of one of my low priority servers, and would then corrupt some of the data on the server, delete other data, and add a great deal of garbage to the server. Finally, I would use the backup I had taken to get the server back to the backed up state. The representative I spoke with at Acronis gave me a trial license, and the results were impressive. The server was restored EXACTLY to the state in which it was backed up. The only other product I've seen that worked this well was Symantec Ghost, but Symantec does a terrible job keeping their product line up to date with current operating systems and hardware. Acronis True Image backup is updated frequently.

Having said this, you should know that if you're using Acronis True Image to upgrade from a smaller hard drive to a larger hard drive, it will work, but it will not automatically increase the partition size to the entire size of the new hard drives. If your old hard drive was 100 GB large, the partition size on the new hard drive will also be 100 GB large, with a bunch of unused free space. Acronis sells their Disk Director product to extend the C:\ drive to the entire size of the hard drive. This is probably the ONLY area that Symantec Ghost bests Acronis True Image.

Finally, Acronis has always had an issue with their new product versions. You can almost always count on the new version of their products to have numerous bugs for the first month or two. Acronis works hard to build in a lot of new features, but these new features often introduce bugs that sometimes make the product unusable for that first month or two. They always release updates and patches that fix these bugs, but it's often best to wait a few months before purchasing a new version of their product, or before upgrading from an older full version to a newer version (e.g. Acronis True Image 2011 to Acronis True Image 2012). Starting with their 2011 or 2012 version, Acronis True Image now has the option at installation time to check for and download a newer version that what was purchased, and you should always do this, so it fixes any problems with the software.

Overall, I love the Acronis line of products. For personal use, you can't beat the Acronis True Image line of products.

For example - people tell me they miss the start menu... When the release day came I was curious, so I went to the Windows 8 webpage and there they had an \\"upgrade offer\\" for $39.99..how could I pass that up, that is such a good deal!!
I was getting sick of Vista Ultimate 64 constantly cranking my HD and getting slower and slower as each month would go by, so we took the plunge.
Worried by all the negative hype I didn't know what to expect.
The upgrade took about 30 minutes, it went smoothly and all my applications including Adobe CS6 function smoothly and are 100% stable.

So lets go over some important points:

Stability..superb
Speed: using the Heaven DX11/ UniEngine Benchmark tool my PC went from ( in Vista 64 Ultimate) 56 to 61 average FPS to a jaw dropping average 101 to 112 FPS, almost 50% increase!! That alone should have gamers seriously consider this OS

The Metro Interface disaster or impossible to navigate??
Actually none of those things, after about a hour of fooling around, looking at a few videos on YouTube, I found the navigation from the Metro to Desktop a breeze, the visual appeal plus the fullscreen apps were really thoughtfully done and have lots of depth to them, impressive.

My only complaint is that \\" games\\" and \\" music\\" you are \\"funneled\\" by Microsoft to use or feel your forced to use Xbox music or games, same with the Mail account, Microsoft forces you to use a Hotmail/ Live account for your email and sign in, for me thats a big turn off .But then again, Microsoft has been doing that for a long time, just this time around you can't help but feel your arm being twisted.

In the end, I found that all the horror stories and negativity to be unfounded nonsense, the usual moaning and groaning that happens when a company ventures into a different direction.
Conclusion: Microsoft has taken a risky and bold step towards something imaginative, bravo.
Apart from the appearance and navigation, the performance of Windows 8 Pro 64, is absolutely impressive.
Ignore the negative hype like you would the noise of rush hour traffic!!

review_body:
Just DL'd Shadow 5. It may do a good job of backing up--I don't know yet--but just the setup routine, and the parent company itself, raise some serious doubts about using their product.

Since I'm unaware of any other auto-backup programs, I've still been using DataKeeper from Power Quest, but it's iffy on XP (needs baby-sitting to make sure the auto backups really work correctly), and I doubt it's any better under Win 7 (the new computer I'm building is Win 7 64 bit). Can't blame Power Quest, though, as they went out of business a few years back, and so DataKeeper was never revised for XP. I absolutely loved it on Win 2K, however...every time I created a new file, DataKeeper backed it up automatically, on the fly.

But NTI came along with Shadow 5, which seems to do much the same thing as DataKeeper, so I DL'd it today, wanting to get the backup in Shadow 5's format before transferring the backup and data drives to the new machine.

The first thing one notices in trying to set up Shadow 5 is that if you have questions, there is no manual (either hard copy or even pdf) to give you an overall view of the program. The auto setup that start initially on its own wanted to back up to an 8MB pin drive, so I found a box for \\"Advanced\\" setup, which did allow me to individually select my choice of drives to back up to, and folders to back up. When I got to step two, there was a list of drives in a window, but not one letter of text explaining what to do with that screen. I had been keeping my eye out for a place to actually select my target drive, and suspected this screen might have something to do with that, but I sure wasn't going to select a drive on a whim, click \\"next\\" and see what happened without a bit more information.

So I had to call NTI.(No 800 numbers here, boys and girls, it's a toll call to California for this cheap company if you want to actually discuss the issue.) Or, you could use their message screen to get email help. But it's a bit of a drawback that the text window you type in doesn't scroll when you run out of space, it just keeps typing without scrolling down. So you have to manually scroll down after each line you type if you want to see what you're doing. (No, you can't scroll down several lines in advance, just one line at a time after the cursor drops to start placing type on the next line below the border!)

Anyway, the tech told me on the phone that the screen I was on (screen 2)tells me at the top to select the drive from the list for my target drive. Since it did no such thing, she brought it up on her screen to see for herself, and was surprised to see that indeed, there were no instructions for anything on that page.

So, to recap so far, they left out a crucial bit of information at step two, and the tech obviously hadn't even seen the page to know about this issue. They can't design a usable email tech support window that scrolls normally. Tech support isn't even familiar with the program they're supporting. No toll-free tech support calls. Are you starting to get a good picture of NTI's competence and attitude toward its customers so far? What if they check their program code as closely as they check the user interface? (Oops! Sorry you lost all your data--we forgot a line of code!)

I wish there were other auto-backup programs around, but I don't know of any. If there were, I'd gladly take a loss on my $40 to get away from NTI as quickly as I could.

review_headline: For immersion, go with L-Lingo, Rosetta Stone is a rip-off
review_body:
There are many different ideas on the best way for adults to learn a foreign language. Much depends on the student, their goals, and their self-discipline. Dealing with a tonal language, like Thai, or a language with a different type of script, also like Thai, the student need make some big decisions about how they want to learn, and how much.

I learned Spanish as an adult. I am now fluent at a professional/business level.

I learned to read Thai. I can write some, but my vocabulary is very small. 90% of my Thai came from taking private one-on-one classes while living in Thailand for 6 months.

I studied some Tagalog, some Korean, and some Thai using Rosetta Stone.

If you just want to learn some Thai to get around as a tourist, you probably want to use Romanized phonetics. Learning the script is not really worth your time. An immersion product, like Rosetta Stone, is probably not as useful because much of the vocabulary and context is not related to what you will want to know (do you really need to say the boy is under the soccer ball?).

If you want to seriously learn the language to be able to carry on casual or business conversations, commit early and realize there is far more work.

For me, I first needed to learn the alphabet. You CANNOT consistently pronounce Thai correctly using Romanized phonetics. T one rules are only consistent in Thai script. Among other challenges, the Romanization is wildly inconsistent. You learn it one way, and then another source using different phonetics mires you in confusion. The same is probably also true of Korean, as it is also a phonetic language. Learning Chinese will likely be different.

Second, I realized for me, I need to take notes. As adults we want to take notes to help remember key points. If you take the notes in English, you are handicapping yourself. Learn the alphabet and take notes in Thai. Again, I think this is true for phonetic languages like Korean, or even Hirigana and Katakana for Japanese. I doubt this is viable for Chinese.

Third, again for me, I knew learning translation would create a permanent handicap. Early on, translation is easier, later on translation msut be unlearned as it stilts actual conversation and thinking. You just can't translate fast enough. Even now, being fluent in Spanish, translating gives me a headache and frustrates me. I either have a conversation in Spanish, thinking in Spanish, or I have a conversation in English thinking in English. If I know a word in one language and not the other, my whole train of thought is derailed. Avoiding learning translation is where Rosetta Stone shines.

I like the idea of Rosetta Stone. If you are disciplined and do the lessons, you will expand your spoken vocabulary rapidly. You will remember what you learn. I doubt it will do much for reading and writing with non-Roman scripts. Like any learning tool, disciplined study will yield results.

Rosetta Stone is very expensive. Competing products like L-Lingo or products using different methods like Pimsleur, TellMeMore.com, Assimil, or Fluenz (supposedly the best, but only in a few languages) are a fraction of the cost of Rosetta Stone. Many of the different methods will work better for some people than others. Assimil is translation based. Pimsleur is hard to describe, but has a very good fluency success rate (supposedly). Look up Fluenz also, as the method and reviews suggest it is very effective in the few languages they offer.

Besides cost, what is the other drawback to Rosetta Stone?

The drawbacks are legion.

Version 2 is good. Version 2 is how Rosetta Stone grew into a powerhouse. Version 3 is a refinement of version 2 with improved continuity, a smoother interface, better quizzes, and the ability to get rid of the stupid \\"must have CD with you at all times\\" limitation.
The real problem is Rosetta Stone dropped support for version 2. Even though they were selling version 2 from their own website in 2012, they dropped support. Mac users are especially impacted as Mac OSX Lion will no longer run PPC apps, and Rosetta Stone never ported the Version 2 application to Intel. So, if you bought version 2 in 2012 to use on a Mac, you were ripped off by Rosetta Stone. Join the crowd.

Windows users should not be too smug about the situation, as the end of Version 2 support means your product will have all sorts of issues too, unless you downgrade to WinXP.

Version 3 (never made for Thai) does run on current platforms, and is at least somewhat supported (to the extent Rosetta Stone supports any product). Given so many users prefer version 3 to version 4 though, don't be surprised if they pull a Microsoft and force you to their new product nobody wants.

Total 4e (not an option for Thai), is a horrible retrograde of Rosetta Stone. The pinnacle is by far version 3. To be fair, if you are always connected -- literally 100% of the time -- and live your life via social media, Total 4e might be effective. Don't expect to use the highly touted iOS apps on your iPhone or iPad though unless you are connected either. The whole idea of quickly practicing while in line or waiting in an office...yeah, that doesn't conform to the Rosetta Stone licensing model.

Speaking of which, Rosetta Stone now has two components and two licensing models. There is the online social media part, and the software application. The first is now on a subscription basis. You pay for every month you learn. You can still use the app on your computer, but you just paid a premium for online access you aren't using. I have spend roughly 12 of those years as a network analyst working on routers, switches, firewalls, intrusion prevention amongst other technologies. This is quite possibly the worst product I have ever seen. For starters, Microsoft SMB (tcp 139 and 445) ports are left open. These are the most sought after ports by hackers on the internet and they allow inbound access by default out of the box. In addition, SQL and Microsoft access, database link, ports are left open inbound. NetBios ports by default are left open. To top it all off, if you change these settings they will mysteriously return to the default configuration (which includes have the IPS turned off) rendering the firewall and IPS totally useless. There is simply no excuse for this type of carelessness in a product made by a reputable manufacturer. If you want an antivirus, check out Avast or AVG for free. The security portion of this......firewall will simply make you more vulnerable to hackers than if you simply ran the windows firewall by itself, which this product disables by the way.

I've been using Quicken since the mid-1990's and I have always been a big Quicken fan until this release. Prior to this release, Quicken was the tool I used used to manage my finances and keep things under control. With this release, Quicken has \\"revamped\\" the budget section to make it unusable. They have removed the ability to modify budget entries for prior months and force the user to evaluate a budget on the upcoming rolling 12 months. So, let's say you budget $1,000 per year for home repairs. For the old method, you created a budget in January and entered into your budget that you planned on spending $1,000 per year on this category. If March came around and you spent the $1,000 in that month, with the old method you could change the annual amount and put the amount into a single month - in this case March - so your reports would show you're on track. Furthermore, you could make this change, plan and track where you were on a calendar year basis. Quicken 2012 doesn't allow this. Now, you can only change budget amounts for the current month and those in the future plus you can evaluate any changes based on the current year. So you can adjust a 2012 budget to allocate more for groceries and less for gas mid-way through the year AND see that your total for 2012 will be unchanged. These application changes make Quicken 2012 worthless for me - I can no longer keep track of my finances and see how I'm tracking in the current year. Moreover, Quicken carries forward budget entries into the next calendar year - a HUGE assumption by Quicken. I may have budgeted $500 for tires in February of this year but that doesn't mean I plan to spend that amount every February.

Who wrote this stuff? Software programmers or people that actually use this stuff? Whatever happened to the people that made Quicken great?

Stick with Quicken 2011 or find another program - I'm sorry to say.

Likely best to get that out of the way before letting One Step Update do anything after the upgrade. 5) Afterwards, having been alerted a One Step Update had previously been missed, I did a One Step Update, and it now works on one bank with which it had trouble before. 6) In the lower right corner of the One Step Update window there was an alert about a further upgrade to release 3 being available, so I then installed that. Overall, a lengthy but not painful process.

The layout of the software windows is so deceivingly simple that you may think you can use the software right out of the box, but this isn't so, unless you've tried another version of the software. Figuring out the software isn't wholly intuitive, and you'll need to give yourself time to master it. If you're new to it, I recommend trying out the character wizard first, just so you can quickly see the types of animations you will eventually be able to create (this is on p. 366-386 in the Pro manual).

The professional version of this title allows users access to a few more set animations for pre-made characters (such as jumping and waving), access to more output formats, and other advanced features, including a 3D look in addition to the basic 2D. The two main changes that will make a big difference in selecting if this product is for you, I feel, relate to the time and audio specs. Even basic users may wish to purchase this title instead, due to the limitations that the Debut version has in these two areas.

First, animation length is unlimited in the Pro version of the software. In the Debut title, animations are limited to a very short two minutes. I found a workaround for this in making shorter \\"scenes,\\" and then splicing the mini-videos together in a separate program to create a 30 minute cartoon, so it's entirely possible to make longer cartoons from the Debut version when used in conjunction with an additional piece of outside software, but it takes a lot more patience to set up the scenes again and again, and it can be a time-crunch challenge to fit within two minutes. In the Pro version, an animation can continue on as long as is necessary.

Second, in the Debut version, only two audio tracks can be used in each animation. That means that if you have a cartoon with two characters, each can speak only one time (or, one character can speak two times). Any characters over two will have to remain silent in Debut. This is extremely limiting to any animation. I did find a bit of a workaround for timing things properly--you can keep a live audio throughout the entire animation for two characters and then attempt to time it right so that no character is overlapping the other, and they can have a normal give-and-take conversation. Doing this is not easy and involves a lot of guesswork. The Pro version has no audio track limits, so it's much easier to create audio cartoons, rather than merely visual animations. You can have one character talk and lip synch it, have another talk and lip synch it to that character, and so on.

As with the Debut version, the software doesn't show animations at their full glory until they are exported or previewed. (I.e., the program window is a lower-quality version of the animation.) I wish this had somehow been different in the Pro version, although it would probably be far too memory-intensive for systems to keep up with a final version in the preview window.

It's hard to imagine becoming anywhere near fluent without the rules and such, but I'm reviewing Level 1, so that's not for me to say.
The headset is very nice and solid. So why does each new level come with one?? What a waste! Offer the option of buying the software and using the headset we have.

review_headline: Now costs extra for media player

About a year ago I cancelled my cable tv and bought a tuner that was designed to use with windows media center that came with the Windows 7 software on my computer. While I had a bit of trouble getting the digital over the air signal, a new outside antenna fixed that problem and between my Amazon Prime and Hulu Plus, I've been a very happy camper!

The other day I bought a new laptop so that my mother in law could watch tv in her room and it came with Windows 8. I read up on this new program and NOWHERE did I see that they were doing away with Windows Media Player! So, I go to set it up and it's not there!

I called Microsoft to see where it was and was informed that it would now cost me an extra $99.00 to upgrade so that I could have the media player. I griped and they then told me that I could upgrade to Windows 8 \\"Pro\\" for $39,99. I didn't see where I should have to pay more for a lessor program, so I requested that they swap the windows 8 out for windows 7 and then we could call it a day.

Nope, can't do that! They told me that I would have to contact Toshiba.

Maybe I'm wrong, but watching tv was the specific reason that we bought that computer and I don't see why I should have to \\"upgrade\\" in order to get the same functionality that the older program had...aren't we supposed to be moving forward???

I've now been waiting for a couple of hours for a supervisor from Microsoft to call me back and am two thirds towards running over to the Apple store and buying a Mac (which I've confirmed can be used to watch over the air tv with the purchase of a usb turner.)

To say that I'm disappointed in Microsoft would be an understatement. VERY POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE!

Update...I still haven't heard back from the supervisor, so I called Microsoft's corporate number (425-882-8080) and asked to speak with the executive resolution group (or at least someone without a headset on) and was told that I would have to email them after giving them my personal information. I then asked if I could speak with the VP in charge of customer service and they refused to tell me who that was...so, I googled it and found an Blog post by a lady named Barbara Gordon where she slams google's customer service and compliments Microsoft's.

I called the corporate office back and asked for Ms. Gordon's office and was told that I would have to initiate my correspondence via the US mail (really?? One of the world's largest technology companies and I have to send them a letter??? Seems like a stiff arm to me!

review_headline: Powerful image editor; remains feature-dense (and *really* wants you online for Adobe services!)...
review_body:
Photoshop Elements (PSE) 10 --like its predecessor versions-- is an image editor with a spectrum of features that will rapidly surpass the skills (and time available to tinker) of most amateur digital photographers...even highly skilled ones. The overall interface will be familiar to user of PSE versions as far back as PSE 6 or 7. It incorporates most of the multiple image merge functions familiar to users since PSE 7. As with previous versions, PSE 10 offers this for a fraction of the cost of its big-brother [[ASIN:B003B32B2I Photoshop CS5]]. Most amateur photographers --and even some frugal professionals-- can perform all but the most advanced digital editing with PSE 10 (and then use the money saved for some nice new hardware!).

Note: This review assumes some familiarity with digital photography and digital image concepts, and previous exposure to earlier PSE versions.

Installation:
-No issues with installation on a machine with a fresh (less than two weeks old) install of Windows 7, a dual-core 3 GHZ processor and 4 GB of RAM.

-Unlike PSE 8, PSE 10 does not require users to decide whether to continue using an earlier version or use the new version exclusively. You have the option to use --or remove-- both version 10 and an earlier version (but you can't do so at the same time: I tried!).

-The license for this product permits installation on one primary and one \\"mobile\\" computer, with the restriction not to use on both computers at the same time.

-Total installation time (including entering the registration code and skimming the EULA) took less than 10 minutes. This was followed by PSE 10's \\"Organizer\\" peforming its own indexing of the digital images on my computer. Cataloging nearly 50,000 digital images took slightly less than an hour. If you're a Windows user and store your images in a non-default \\"My Pictures\\" location under your user name: you'll have to tell PSE where to browse for this indexing.

Function and features:
-The interface, function and features of PSE 10 will be familiar to users of recent PSE versions. The .psd files are still manipulated using layers and selection tools. The complete range of image effects (\\"filters\\"), image enhancement and editing tools are essentially unchanged since version 6. Still present are options to open, edit and save in wide range of file formats.

-PSE 10 recognized the scanner on my system, and immediately allowed imports of scanned images using both the scanner's proprietary interface (Epson software) and the generic WIA Windows Image Acquisition, the successor to TWAIN) options.

-Output to the printers on my system was trouble-free. Accepting the default printing options yielded fine results, but advanced options for those who like to tweak are readily available. PSE 10 successfully offered options to print to the two physical (laserjet, inkjet) and two virtual (Acrobat and Microsoft Document Writer) printers attached to my desktop.

Issues:
-PSE 10 and Adobe continue to assume plenty about user connectivity. All of the help files for PSE 10 are online. Select \\"Help\\" in the menu bar (or press the \\"F1\\" key), and you are not taken to local help files...you are taken to adobe.com. This is fine if you are connected to the Internet, but less fine if you are not (and some people are NOT connected at all times). You can optionally download a 27 MB .pdf user guide. This is an option you'll want to exercise if you anticipate needing help while not online or if you have bandwidth constraints where you work.

-Adobe also continues to also push its online services hard. At install, and *every* time you launch PSE 10, you will be invited to enter your \\"Adobe Online ID\\". If you register (and you'll probably want to just for update notifications), you'll get some free services (2 GB of storage and some sharing functions). This seems to be aimed at two things:
(1) tracking use habits of users (my opinion only; but read the EULA carefully!)
(2) enticing you into the $49.99 per year \\"PSE 10 Plus\\" services (20 GB of online storage and some sharing and effects services). While I suppose the integration with PSE is nice, you can register your own domain --with unlimited storage-- from hundreds of providers for much less than this. Resist!

As long as you download the .pdf file so you have access to help files when offline, and remain aware of what *any* software company may be doing when they solicit you to use the online extensions of their products: these are not serious shortcomings. But my suspicions about how Adobe might track user behavior and over-reliance on online help files are what move this from a 5-star to a 4-star review.

Finally:
-PSE 10, like all of its predecessors is feature dense. Even powerful users will benefit from additional help. In addition to widely available online forums (hosted by Adobe and elsewhere on the web; search popular video sites for step-by-steps on even the most advanced functions), a reference book will improve your user experience. Remember: technology is complicated, and you're not a dummy! Rather than something in yellow and black that calls you names, consider the [[ASIN:1449398502 Photoshop Elements 10 \\"Missing Manual\\"]] instead.

My copy shipped with a $20 gift card for online printing services from Shutterfly (available with any purchase of $20 or more), a trial version of [[ASIN:B005MMMT3W Adobe Premiere Elements 10]] (for video editing; $79 to activate), which installed concurrently (and optionally) with PSE 10. I have a functional earlier version of Premier Elements, so just uninstalled this trial version. Also included in this package was an installation CD for a 30-day trial of [[ASIN:B003739DVY Lightroom 3]], which I did not install.

The physical media for PSE 10 consists of thee 3 DVDs, One is for Windows users (Disc 1), one for Mac users (Disc 3). I was never prompted to do anything with the mysterious \\"Disc 2\\"; perhaps it is Mac-unique?

PSE 10 is a powerful image editing tool priced right for consumers. Purchase with confidence. Is it worth upgrading from version 8 or 9? Probably not. review_headline: Simply the best software/resource I've found.
review_body:
It's hard for me to overstate the help I've gotten from this program in learning Japanese. I'm someone who has never done well with languages in a classroom setting. For some reason, my brain doesn't seem to jive well with the way most foreign language teachers teach. Nothing sinks in, concepts don't 'click', and after I somehow pass the class, I forget everything.

That's what nearly happened when I took Japanese 100 in college last semester. The class would simply whizz by while I can honestly say I learned next to nothing. Finally, the week of finals, I decided I needed to do something to get up to speed so I'd pass. I used Human Japanese for a few days and learned more than I did during the whole semester. Not only that, but the program helped me to realize just how simple some of the concepts were.

While textbooks tend to describe things in technical-speak that would confuse my understanding even of my native language, Human Japanese does what the name suggests and what the developer promises: it explains Japanese in a personal, human way that does wonders for teaching the new language to someone. I can't tell you how many times I finished learning a new concept and was surprised at just how simple it had been. This program inspires confidence in your ability to learn Japanese. It doesn't take off and leave you in the dust anywhere, ever.

We use Rosetta Stone at school, and I literally hate the program. Never mind its price, Human Japanese is a far superior program for learning the basics of Japanese. The fact that it's much, much more affordable is a huge bonus. Keep in mind, Human Japanese has just released a follow-up program called Human Japanese Intermediate for people who have finished the original and want to delve further into the language. It has been released for iPad thus far, and will come to PC/Mac/iPhone/etc soon. I can't wait!

I have filters to delete all files in c:\Documents and Settings/[user]/Local Settings/Temp that are NOT text files. Also allows you to do a partial restore. I had a user get a nasty email virus (new as of that day) and while Windows System Restore didn't help, restoring from the VCOM Checkpoint restored the computer to working order while also removing the (well hidden) virus. - Move You can back up any installed application - files and registry items - and create an installation package that you can use to install on a new computer. DMPE (essentially version 11.0)is most definitely a significant downgrade compared to DNS Medical v. 10.1. DMPE was an 80% rewrite of the entire program, and not surprisingly introduced problems. Many physicians that \\"upgraded\\" from DNS Medical v. 10.1 to DMPE later truly upgraded by ditching DMPE and going back to DNS Medical v. 10.1. Also keep in mind that dictating is only part of the equation of efficiency, and using commands to facilitate EMR navigation and multi-step processes while minimizing clicks and keyboard use is equally if not more important. Also, keep in mind that using a version other than a medical version does not allow direct dictation into an EMR. Nuance has a \\"hit list\\" of EMRs and the microphone will be turned-off trying to use non-medical (less expensive) versions.

product_title: TextAloud With AT&T Natural Voices (Windows Software)
review_body:
After spending time with NaturalReader, I wanted to see how it compared with other text-to-speech software. What do you know; I found a program called TextAloud.

Other than different user interfaces, these two pieces of software worked fairly the same. Both versions offer the same voices: One female and one male. I stuck with the male voice. The male voice sounded a bit more natural while the female voice sounded like a computer (chunky).

One thing I did like about the NaturalReader was the ability to use it in MS Word. I loved it. It made editing far easier. Rather than the copy and paste back and forth, all my work was done directly within my Word document. Kudos!

I ran into one glitch while using TextAloud. It happened at the exact same place in my document every time. Each time it hit one particular line, the program froze. No where else...just one particular place in my Word document. I ended up closing down the program through task manager and the document before being able to use the product again. I guess that's great for developers, since I can duplicate it; makes it easier to identify the bug.

As for customer service: The creators Nextup.com have a forum for customer support and advice. Though I didn't use it, I did browse it. The monitors are quick to answer questions and offer suggestions.

One thing I didn't like about TextAloud which annoyed the heck out of me was the popup every time I copied something. It didn't matter which document, from the web, where ever, it pulled a little pop up in the lower right hand corner. Grrr! I found a check box in the options section to suppress it, thankfully. So no need to experience the frustration I did.

So what was the deal with the popups? TextAloud has a feature that allows the user to insert the copied text into the TextAloud main software which can be viewed at a later date. Pretty nifty feature if you ask me. There's certainly a time and place for it though it irritated me at first.

Honestly, I didn't really like either voice which came with TextAloud or NaturalReader and could see going with a different voice these products.or it though it irritated me at first.

They have some nice slots but the presentation is AWFUL.  in the previous games each machine was unique.  you got to see the actual machine, the ticket paper slide into it, and out when you cashed out.  all of that is GONE.  this game looks worse than the free slot games you play on facebook, really its that bad!  every slot looks the same.  the lazy programmers created a generic cookie cutter interface for all the slots and the only thing that changes is the actual tiles, but the buttons you press to spin, your credit count, etc is all the same except for a minor color change or background.  in the previous games each slot had its own buttons like the real machine in the casino.  it was like you actually had the machine in front of you, now I don't even recognize that I'm playing real machines.  plus the previous ones had great sound/music: sounds of coins coming out, ambient noise of other machines around you, background noise etc.  now each slot is devoid of almost any music/sound effects.  when you don't spin the game is COMPLETELY silent, no sense of being in a casino or anything.  i was bored playing all of these slots as theyall look similar except for a minor swap of the tiles that spin which is a shame as they included some good slots I've seen in the Casinos.  For how large the game is, the steep system requirements you would think it would be at least as good as the last IGT slots.  Any of the previous IGT slots is better than this which is such a shame since I enjoyed the others so much.  I hope they fire this developer or programmers and hire back the original ones.  If you want a new set of slots look at WMS Slots Zeus II from Phantom EFX, lower system requirements, tons of customizable options to help it run on lower end machines, great music/sound effects and even challenges/achievements to give you a reason to keep playing(like rewarding you for playing by unlocking new machines to play).  Avoid this mess,  its not that its terrible if you haven't played any slot game before but its an embarrassment if your product from 4 years ago looks and plays better than this, you'd be better off playing the free online facebook slots which have better graphics, sounds music than this embarrassment.

I just finished a preliminary tax return and below are my observations. Note: the forms are not final until January 10, 2013.
Note that I purchased H&R Block Deluxe plus State, and in this review I am including only the review of the federal forms. The federal forms part of the product are identical, of course, whether one buys the State add-on or not.

1. H&R Block starts the interview process with an annoying up-sell pitch, recommending an upgrade from Deluxe to Premium even when it is not necessary.
It would have better if they waited until the financial information is entered and offered the Premium version only to those for whom it might make sense.

What is the difference between Premium and Deluxe? The Premium version offers advanced tools for self-employed and rental property owners: cost basis of home sales, dividents, gifts, and inheritance assets. It has advanced schedule C guidance to maximize deductions for self-employment income. And finally it has guidance for rental property income and expenses. The rest of the Premium package is the same as Deluxe.

Note that the Deluxe package has support for self-employed income as well as stock sale cost basis calculations. This year I had to do both, and I found the guidance to be sufficient to complete the forms.

2. As of 11/19/2012 videos for tax law changes were not available yet (the prompt said coming soon).

3. Minor pet peeve: Help is not context sensitive. For example, when you click on \\"learn more\\" about a particular topic the general help window opens but it does not show help topics for the specific topic that you were working on. Instead you need to search and know which words to use locate the relevant topics.

4. Good news: DeductionPro 2012 is now integrated into H&R Block, you no longer need to go to H&R web site.

5. H&R Block provides you some guidance for completing Form 1116 (foreign tax credit, for example from mutual funds). However, you need to keep switching between whole-form view to enter data and then back to interview to read the instructions. Even though the form where you can enter data is visible at the same time as instructions you cannot enter data into it until you switch into whole-form view. This is cumbersome, but at least there is some guidance for this form.

6. Copy and Paste from Interview screens is not possible. Sometimes I wish to do it for some issue as a reminder to myself. My solution is to do PrintScreen (holding ctl key, shift key, and PrintScreen key at the same time). This generates an image of the screen, which I paste into paint or photo editing software which I can print or save for later.

7. I don't use the default location for the tax returns due to how I set up my backup software. The H&R Block software does not initially remember this new location on the second start of the application, it told me I have no returns. I needed to pick the return manually from the File menu, as it did remember recently used files. The third time I started the software, it finally knew the location of the taxreturn file.

8. I use large font option on my monitor display and in the past had display issues (some things were displayed on top of each other). This year all forms displayed properly with this option. Nice!

9. H&R Block Deluxe entitles you to 5 free federal state e-files.

10. The price on this package changes day to day. I found a nice tools that shows history of Amazon prices. If you enter \\"price history alert\\" in Google it will come up at the top, it has the word camel in the name. I find this tool very helpful. I just looked up that the price last year fluctuated between $20 and the list price of $44.99. During the tax preparation season it hit the $20 mark on three different dates. You can set up an alert tool to email you when your desired price has been reached.

11. A note for those who might want to use the digital download rather than the boxed edition
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This year I am using a boxed edition of the software. Last year I used a digital download and run into a glitch a solution to which I want to include again for those who might run into the same issue this year.

After I installed the software and started it for the first time it prompted me to enter a key-code. The prompt said that I should have received in the email after purchasing the software, however the email I received from Amazon did not contained a key-code. I had to call Amazon support and they told me that this information can be found following these steps
1) Log into Amazon
2) Select Your Account at the top right of the page
3) Select Games and Software downloads which is towards the bottom of the long page you see when you log in
4) Then under H&R software entry you will see the key-code that you need to enter to unlock the software

12. Update 12/10/2012. I received a question if H&R allows to install the software on two PCs. I found the answer on H&R Block web site FAQ under the topic \\"Installing Software on Another Computer\\"

There are just a few steps necessary to re-install the H&R Block At Home program from the CD you received in the mail. Follow the steps below to re-install the program or install it on a second computer.
Insert the H&R Block At Home CD into your computer.
Click the Need to Re-install? link on the menu bar at the bottom of the screen.
The Frequently Asked Questions page will open to the first FAQ titled, \\"Can I install the software on a second computer?\\"
Enter your activation code and last 4 digits of the credit card you used to purchase the program initially and click Activate.
You can find your activation code in your purchase confirmation e-mail.
Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the installation.

13. Update 12/18/2012. Adding another answer to great question to share with everyone.
Q: Is there an audit check which marks problems with red flags?
A: At the end of the interview process there is a check step (which you can run at any time, but the interview ends with this check). This step flags problems (e.g. missing information) and potential audit alerts (e.g. unusual deductions) with red flags , and reminders (e.g. things you marked tentative) with yellow flags.

14. Update 2/7/2013. I received a question if I had any problem doing updates of the software.
I have performed several updates without problems. If you have a firewall, the firewall prompts with a question if you trust the software and you need to reply \\"yes\\". If you say no, the install will be rolled back. If you accidentally reply \\"No\\" to this prompt, I would recommend uninstalling the software. Then installing it again, and then trying another update. Alternatively you can deactivate the firewall during the install.

review_headline: Lots of Fun, Medium Difficulty, Moderate Length!
review_body:
This game is a lot of fun and I got a kick out of the storyline. You are Kate Reed, author of supernatural novels. It's a dark and dreary night. Kate has fallen asleep at her desk, but she's awakened by the doorbell ringing. She goes to the door, but there's no one there, only a package left on the porch. She opens the package and it's an old-fashioned typewriter. Your first inventory based puzzle is to do some assembly on the typewriter, which then types out a message by itself! Kate is invited to a seance.

The problem is, the house in which the seance is located is cursed. It periodically changes locations, simply disappears from one location and sets down in another. You never know where it will land next. Worse, if you don't get out by the next time it changes location, you'll be stuck in the house forever.

When you start a game, you are asked if you want to play the casual version or expert version. The differences are that in the casual version, points of interaction, such as where you can pick up an object, are highlighted. Also, the built-in hint system takes 1 minute to reload in casual, versus two minutes in expert.

Even in the expert version, you are given lots of hints when Kate talks to herself. For example, when you click on the typewriter, a caption appears saying, "I need paper to put in the typewriter". A more difficult game would require that you figure that out without the game telling you.

This Collector's Edition also has a Strategy Guide built right in, with screen shots of every scene and complete answers to every puzzle and inventory-based action as well as location of each hidden object. To access the strategy guide, you exit the game to the Main Menu. From the Main Menu, select Strategy Guide. You may not need the guide, though, due to the game's built-in hint system and low-to medium difficulty of the puzzles and inventory-based actions.

I counted 29 hidden object screens, 14 pure puzzles (all of which can be skipped), and many many inventory based actions in the regular game. In this collector's edition, you're given an extra chapter of fun for even more of all three types of action: 7 HO screens, 4 puzzles, and multitudes of inventory actions! My personal preference is for PC games that are a little heavier on the number of puzzles, compared to hidden object, with a bit more difficulty in the puzzles and inventory actions, which is why I gave Family Secrets four stars instead of five. But don't get me wrong, this is still a fun game.

Comparing it to similar styled games, I thought [[ASIN:B006W41WF0 House of 1,000 Doors: Family Secrets - Collector's Edition]] was more difficult than [[ASIN:B0023RTCWA Samantha Swift 2 and the Golden Touch]], less difficult than [[ASIN:B001Q54VVC Mystery Case Files: Return to Ravenhearst]], and the same difficulty as [[ASIN:B003SEIKXO Midnight Mysteries 2: Salem Witch Trials]].

I played on a PC XP. I loaded the game from the CD ROM, and thereafter played without inserting the disc. It took three tries to get it to load, but once loaded, I had no glitches.

A sequel is coming out in May, 2012, [[ASIN:B007XO8W6K House of 1,000 Doors: Palm of Zoroaster (Collector's Edition)]].
.

Added Later, 10/13: A 3rd in the series has been issued. "House of 1,000 Doors: Serpent Flame". I gave the Collector's Edition 5 stars!
